meta.title: F1 2026 Season Tracker — underlying dataset

sources.trackOutlineGeometry: https://github.com/bacinger/f1-circuits (MIT licensed GeoJSON, satellite/GPS-traced, reprojected to a 200x120 SVG viewBox)

notes: teams/drivers/tracks/calendar are the season-long static reference data.
raceResults (keyed by round number) is the per-weekend results data (Grand Prix + sprint where applicable); this is what the in-app Update tab edits.
trackOutlinePaths contains the real traced SVG path 'd' strings per track id, used to render the circuit outlines.

This file reflects the dashboard's built-in defaults as of export. It does NOT include any favorites, predictions, or edits made inside your browser session — for that, use the dashboard's own 'Save file' button, which exports a matching-format JSON plus your personal additions.

teams.name: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
teams.note: Works team since 2010; Mercedes also raced briefly in 1954-55.
teams.storyline2026: Antonelli's rapid rise has Mercedes leading both championships at the season's midpoint, the team's strongest start in years.

teams.name: Scuderia Ferrari HP
teams.note: Founding constructor of the World Championship, racing continuously since 1950.
teams.storyline2026: Hamilton's long-awaited first win for the team came in Barcelona, snapping Mercedes' early winning streak.

teams.name: McLaren Mastercard F1 Team
teams.storyline2026: A difficult title defense so far, including both cars failing to start in China.

teams.name: Oracle Red Bull Racing
teams.engine: Red Bull Ford DM01 (works, new PU brand for 2026)
teams.note: Founded 2005; introduces its own Red Bull Ford power unit in 2026 after the Honda partnership ended.
teams.storyline2026: The new in-house Red Bull Ford power unit has been a reliability step backward so far in its debut year.
teams.usConnection: Power unit co-developed with Ford Motor Company (United States).

teams.name: Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team
teams.note: Racing as "Aston Martin" since 2021; lineage runs through Jordan/Force India/Racing Point back to 1991.
teams.principal: Adrian Newey (Team Principal & Managing Technical Partner)
teams.storyline2026: A troubled debut for the new Honda works partnership — the AMR26 has struggled with power-unit reliability, and Newey's leadership role has been the subject of ongoing succession speculation since March 2026.

teams.name: BWT Alpine F1 Team
teams.note: Racing as "Alpine" since 2021 (Enstone-based lineage since 1986). Switched from Renault to a customer Mercedes power unit in 2026.
teams.principal: Flavio Briatore (Executive Advisor) / Steve Nielsen (Managing Director)
teams.storyline2026: Colapinto's promotion to a full-time seat alongside Gasly has been one of the year's feel-good stories for Alpine's home fans in Argentina.

teams.name: Atlassian Williams F1 Team
teams.note: Founded 1977 by Frank Williams; one of the sport's most successful independent constructors.
teams.storyline2026: Continuing its rebuild under Vowles with a fully customer Mercedes package for 2026.

teams.name: TGR Haas F1 Team
teams.note: Founded 2016; expanded Toyota Gazoo Racing (TGR) partnership prompted a 2026 team rebrand.
teams.hq: Kannapolis, North Carolina, United States (F1 operations: Banbury, United Kingdom)
teams.storyline2026: The expanded Toyota Gazoo Racing partnership prompted the team's 2026 rebrand from Haas to TGR Haas.
teams.usConnection: American-owned (founder Gene Haas); the only originally-American-owned team on the grid besides Cadillac.

teams.name: Audi Revolut F1 Team
teams.note: Audi's first year as a full works team/engine manufacturer, after acquiring Sauber in 2024 (that chassis lineage has raced since 1993).
teams.storyline2026: Team principal Jonathan Wheatley departed abruptly in March 2026 amid reports he would join Aston Martin; Binotto, previously Head of the Audi F1 Project, stepped up to lead the team through its historic debut season.

teams.name: Cadillac Formula 1 Team
teams.note: 2026 is Cadillac's debut season — the first new team on the grid since Haas in 2016.
teams.hq: Fishers, Indiana, United States (F1 operations: Silverstone, United Kingdom)
teams.storyline2026: F1's newest team, backed by General Motors, fields two former Grand Prix winners in Pérez and Bottas for its debut season.
teams.usConnection: American-owned (General Motors/Cadillac); the first all-new US-backed constructor entry since Haas in 2016.

teams.name: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team
teams.note: Lineage runs Toro Rosso (2006) -> AlphaTauri (2020) -> Racing Bulls (2024-).
teams.storyline2026: Fields the only rookie on the 2026 grid, 18-year-old Arvid Lindblad, who took over Isack Hadjar's seat after his promotion to the senior Red Bull team.

tracks.name: Albert Park Circuit
tracks.chars: Semi-street park circuit; fast, flowing layout with modest overtaking zones.
signatureFeatures: Lakeside setting in Albert Park
Fast Turns 9-10 esses
Tight final chicane onto the pit straight
tracks.whyInteresting: A fast, flowing park circuit that rewards momentum and precision, traditionally F1's season opener.

tracks.name: Shanghai International Circuit
tracks.chars: Long back straight (DRS zone); tricky decreasing-radius Turn 1-3 complex.
signatureFeatures: Decreasing-radius Turn 1-3 'snail' complex
1.2 km back straight
Layout inspired by the Chinese character 'shang'
tracks.whyInteresting: Its huge back straight creates one of the calendar's best overtaking opportunities into Turn 14.

tracks.name: Suzuka Circuit
tracks.chars: Iconic figure-eight layout; high-speed Esses, Spoon Curve and 130R.
signatureFeatures: The only genuine figure-eight track in F1
130R high-speed corner
The 'S' Curves esses
tracks.whyInteresting: Widely rated by drivers as F1's ultimate challenge, thanks to its genuine road-crossing figure-eight layout.

tracks.name: Miami International Autodrome
tracks.chars: Purpose-built circuit around Hard Rock Stadium; street-style low-speed sections mixed with long straights.
signatureFeatures: Built around Hard Rock Stadium
Marina section with an artificial water feature
Long back straight into Turn 17
tracks.whyInteresting: A purpose-built stadium circuit blending street-track technicality with stadium-scale spectacle.

tracks.name: Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve
tracks.chars: Stop-start rhythm; the "Wall of Champions" guards the final chicane exit.
signatureFeatures: Wall of Champions at the final chicane
Built on the man-made Île Notre-Dame
Long pit straight favouring engine power
tracks.whyInteresting: A stop-start island circuit that has ended many a champion's race at its notorious final wall.

tracks.name: Circuit de Monaco
tracks.chars: Tightest, slowest circuit on the calendar; narrow street layout, overtaking is rare.
signatureFeatures: Tunnel section beside the harbour
Casino Square and the tight Fairmont hairpin
Narrowest, slowest street circuit in F1
tracks.whyInteresting: The sport's most famous and unforgiving street circuit, where one mistake can end a race instantly.

tracks.name: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
tracks.chars: Mix of a fast final-sector-style corner and a technical, grippy infield section.
signatureFeatures: Historic fast Turn 3 right-hander
Technical, grip-heavy final sector
F1's long-time pre-season testing venue
tracks.whyInteresting: A well-rounded, traditional test of all-round car performance, long used as F1's benchmark testing track.

tracks.name: Red Bull Ring
tracks.chars: Short lap time, big elevation changes, three long straights favour engine power.
signatureFeatures: Set in the Styrian mountains
Three short straights separated by tight corners
One of the shortest laps on the calendar
tracks.whyInteresting: A compact, scenic mountain circuit where its short lap produces frequent slipstreaming battles.

tracks.name: Silverstone Circuit
tracks.chars: High-speed corners (Copse, Maggotts/Becketts, Stowe); demanding on tyres and confidence.
signatureFeatures: Maggotts/Becketts high-speed esses
Copse corner, taken flat in qualifying trim
Hosted the first-ever F1 World Championship race in 1950
tracks.whyInteresting: The birthplace of the F1 World Championship, famous for its stomach-churning high-speed corners.

tracks.name: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
tracks.chars: Longest track on the calendar; Eau Rouge/Raidillon, huge elevation change, unpredictable weather across the lap.
signatureFeatures: Eau Rouge/Raidillon uphill compression
Longest lap on the F1 calendar
Notoriously changeable Ardennes weather
tracks.whyInteresting: The longest and most physically dramatic lap in F1, where the weather can differ from one corner to the next.

tracks.name: Hungaroring
tracks.chars: Tight and twisty with low average speed — sometimes called "Monaco without the walls".
signatureFeatures: Tight, twisty 'Mickey Mouse'-style layout
Very little overtaking; track position is king
Natural amphitheatre banking for spectators
tracks.whyInteresting: A slow, technical circuit nicknamed "Monaco without the walls", where qualifying position often decides the race.

tracks.name: Circuit Zandvoort
tracks.chars: Narrow, dune-lined layout with banked final corner.
signatureFeatures: Banked Arie Luyendyk Bocht final corner
Narrow, dune-lined seaside layout
Passionate orange-clad home crowd
tracks.whyInteresting: A revived seaside dunes classic with a steeply banked final corner rare anywhere else on the calendar.

tracks.name: Monza Circuit
tracks.chars: "Temple of Speed": lowest-downforce setup on the calendar, long flat-out straights.
signatureFeatures: Parabolica final corner
Lowest-downforce setup of the season
Historic banked-oval remnants beside the modern track
tracks.whyInteresting: F1's "Temple of Speed" — the fastest, lowest-downforce track on the calendar.

tracks.name: Madring
tracks.chars: New street-style circuit around Madrid's IFEMA exhibition centre, debuting in 2026 — exact homologated figures to confirm.
signatureFeatures: Brand-new street-style circuit around the IFEMA exhibition centre
F1's return to Madrid for the first time in decades
Takes over the "Spanish Grand Prix" name from Barcelona
tracks.whyInteresting: A brand-new circuit debuting in 2026 that takes over the Spanish Grand Prix name from Barcelona-Catalunya.

tracks.name: Baku City Circuit
tracks.chars: Longest straight on the calendar into a tight castle-section street layout.
signatureFeatures: Longest straight on the calendar (~2.2 km)
Ultra-tight castle section around Baku's old city walls
Street circuit hugging the Caspian Sea
tracks.whyInteresting: Combines Monaco-style tight streets with the longest straight in F1, producing extreme speed contrasts.

tracks.name: Marina Bay Street Circuit
tracks.chars: Night race under floodlights; high heat and humidity make it physically demanding.
signatureFeatures: F1's first-ever night race (2008)
Extreme heat and humidity — one of the most physically demanding races
Runs past Marina Bay's waterfront skyline
tracks.whyInteresting: F1's original night race, run in brutal heat and humidity around a spectacular waterfront skyline.

tracks.name: Circuit of the Americas
tracks.chars: Steep elevation change into Turn 1; an esses section inspired by Silverstone.
signatureFeatures: Steep uphill blind entry into Turn 1
Esses inspired by Silverstone's Maggotts/Becketts
Sweeping, elevation-rich infield section
tracks.whyInteresting: A modern circuit purpose-built to blend the best corners of classic tracks from around the world.

tracks.name: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
tracks.chars: High altitude thins the air, affecting downforce and engine cooling; stadium section at Turns 12-13.
signatureFeatures: Foro Sol stadium section through a baseball/multi-sport arena
Extreme altitude (over 2,200 m) reduces aerodynamic and engine performance
Long Peraltada-inspired final corner
tracks.whyInteresting: Run at extreme altitude, where thin air fundamentally changes how the cars behave.

tracks.name: Autódromo José Carlos Pace (Interlagos)
tracks.chars: Anticlockwise and undulating, with famously unpredictable weather.
signatureFeatures: Sweeping 'Senna S' at the start, named for the local legend
Anticlockwise, undulating layout
Famously unpredictable weather
tracks.whyInteresting: A short, undulating lap named for Ayrton Senna's home-city corners, notorious for chaotic wet races.

tracks.name: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
tracks.chars: Long straights down the Strip; a night race with cold track temperatures.
signatureFeatures: Runs down the Las Vegas Strip past its casinos
Cold overnight track temperatures despite the desert setting
One of the longest straights on the calendar
tracks.whyInteresting: A glittering Strip-side night race with some of the coldest track temperatures anywhere on the calendar.

tracks.name: Lusail International Circuit
tracks.chars: High-speed, flowing layout raced at night.
signatureFeatures: High-speed, flowing corner sequences
Raced at night under floodlights
Originally built for MotoGP
tracks.whyInteresting: A fast, rhythmic circuit originally designed for motorcycle racing, raced under lights in the desert.

tracks.name: Yas Marina Circuit
tracks.chars: Season-finale venue; race starts in daylight and finishes under lights.
signatureFeatures: Race starts in daylight and finishes under lights
Marina section beside superyachts
Traditional F1 season finale
tracks.whyInteresting: F1's traditional season finale, transitioning from daylight to dusk beside a glittering marina.

1.headline: Russell leads a Mercedes 1-2 in a chaotic season opener
1.recap: George Russell held off a fast-recovering Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton to win the 2026 curtain-raiser, with teammate Kimi Antonelli completing a Mercedes 1-2. Two Virtual Safety Cars and a one-stop strategy gamble shaped a wild afternoon that also saw both McLarens fail to start.

2.headline: Antonelli beats Russell in an all-Mercedes headline act at Shanghai
2.recap: Kimi Antonelli converted pole into his first Grand Prix win, resisting an early challenge from Hamilton and controlling the gap to teammate Russell after the race's only Safety Car. Both McLarens and both Williams cars failed to start due to technical issues.

3.headline: Antonelli completes a hat-trick of wins at Suzuka
3.recap: Kimi Antonelli made it three wins from three races, converting pole to victory at Suzuka ahead of Oscar Piastri and Charles Leclerc. Oliver Bearman's heavy crash brought out the race's only Safety Car.

4.headline: Antonelli holds off Norris for a third straight win
4.recap: Kimi Antonelli survived a three-way scrap at the start and late pressure from Lando Norris to win a Safety-Car-interrupted Miami Grand Prix, extending his perfect start to the season. The race began three hours earlier than scheduled due to forecast storms.

5.headline: Antonelli wins an attrition-heavy Canadian GP
5.recap: Kimi Antonelli extended his championship lead with victory at Montreal ahead of Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen, in a race that claimed 18 retirements. A late Safety Car for the Norris/Piastri collision neutralized the finish after an earlier VSC for Perez's suspension failure.

meta.note: A dramatic weekend: Stroll's crash (lap 60) brought out the first Safety Car; Leclerc crashed at the same corner on the restart, triggering a second Safety Car that became a red flag for track repairs (resurfacing work had broken up at Turn 19); the race then resumed with a Safety Car-led restart lap before a standing start.

6.headline: Antonelli wins a red-flag-interrupted Monaco classic
6.recap: Kimi Antonelli led every lap from pole to claim a fifth straight victory, surviving two Safety Car periods, a red flag for track damage, and a standing restart. Hamilton held on for 2nd as George Russell's afternoon collapsed through penalties.

7.headline: Hamilton ends Mercedes' streak with a maiden Ferrari win
7.recap: Lewis Hamilton claimed his first victory for Ferrari, using a free pit stop under a Virtual Safety Car to beat George Russell and end Mercedes' run of five straight wins. Kimi Antonelli's championship lead was cut after he failed to finish.

8.headline: Russell wins from pole as Antonelli fights back for the fastest lap
8.recap: George Russell controlled the race from pole to beat Max Verstappen, whose hard tyres faded late in the Styrian heat. Kimi Antonelli recovered from an early VSC pit-stop setback to take 3rd and the fastest lap of the race.

9.headline: Leclerc wins under Safety Car after a late Verstappen spin
9.recap: Charles Leclerc took his first win since October 2024 after Max Verstappen spun out with four laps to go, bringing out a Safety Car that ran to the flag. George Russell recovered from a lap-35 puncture-forced pit stop to finish 2nd, gaining 18 points on championship leader Antonelli.

10.headline: Antonelli wins at Spa as Russell crashes out on lap one
10.recap: Kimi Antonelli claimed his sixth win of the season at Spa-Francorchamps, ahead of Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen, after teammate George Russell crashed out on the opening lap following contact with Lewis Hamilton. Hamilton was handed a 5-second penalty for the incident but still finished 4th.
